thread.title: Markets Now: Dow Gains 33 Points as Caterpillar Soars

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Markets Now: Dow Gains 33 Points as Caterpillar Soars
text:
Markets Now: As S&P 500 Slips, Value Stocks Shine July 30, 2018, 08:01:00 AM EDT By Evie Liu, Barron's
Want to know why the Dow Jones Industrial Average is doing what it's doing? Check back here for a semi-live look at the volatile markets from Barron's reporters.
1:04 p.m. After lagging the S&P 500 over the past two years, the value-stock comeback might just be getting started.
The Invesco S&P 500 Pure Value ETF ( RPV ) tracks the least-expensive stocks in the S&P 500 based on book value-to-price ratio, earnings-to-price ratio and sales-to-price ratio. After tumbling throughout June, the Pure Value ETF rose 2.3% last week, approaching $68.11, an important resistance level that it's hit twice this year.
Michael Wilson , chief U.S. equity strategist at Morgan Stanley , argues that now is a good time to shift from growth stocks-the market's fastest growing-to value. Growth stocks have been outperforming value at a rate unseen since the dot-com bubble, but relative forward earnings-per-share growth does not support the big gap between the two, Wilson contends.
Furthermore, sectors have been experiencing rolling bear markets this year, during which almost every group in the S&P 500 has suffered significant losses at one point or another. Right now, S&P 500 leadership has turned defensive, with Utilities and Staples the best performing sectors since June 18.
And it could get worse. Wilson urges investors to prepare for potential correction to come. With most of the big earnings and economic news out of the way, Wilson has already observed signs of "market exhaustion" last week, as the S&P 500 has dropped 1.3% since last Wednesday. "With Amazon's strong quarter out of the way and a very strong 2Q GDP number , investors were finally faced with the question of'what do I look forward to now?'" wrote Wilson in a note today.
Wilson recommends investors add positions of both a defensive sector, Utilities, and value sectors-Energy, Industrials, and Financials-in preparation for a pullback.
The Invesco S&P 500 Pure Value ETF has gained 0.5% to $67.96, while the S&P 500 has dropped 0.6% to 2803.27.
Dow Gains 33 Points as Caterpillar Soars
7:38 a.m. Tech is out, the old economy is in as the market continues to deal with last week's implosion of Facebook ( FB ) and Twitter ( TWTR ) shares. S&P 500 futures have dipped 0.1%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have risen 33 points, or 0.1%. Nasdaq Composite futures have dropped 0.3%. Getty Images
Caterpillar ( CAT ) got the Dow of to a good start Monday morning-it's up 3.1% at $147 after topping earnings forecasts -but tech will remain in focus this week, particularly with Apple ( AAPL ) set to report after Tuesday's close. And don't forget that the Bank of Japan , the U.S. Federal Reserve and the Bank of England are all meeting this week .
That could mean what happens today will have little bearing on where the market finishes this week. - Ben Levisohn
